title: PIPSeq_QCreport pipeline parameters
description: Nextflow wrapper around perturbseq_report -- a Perturb-seq QC and analysis pipeline that turns a sample manifest + .h5ad into a self-contained HTML report.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: manifest is the one thing you must set. h5ad is effectively required too on platforms that don't mount a project's data tree into the task (see its own description). qc_container has a working public default -- only change it if you've rebuilt and pushed your own image.

manifest.help_text: Where results go (output_path is ignored by this pipeline -- see 'outdir' instead). Also carries the optional gRNA/hashtag whitelist paths and, once filled in, the five QC thresholds below. A run that reaches the QC stage writes those thresholds back into this file (with a timestamped backup made first), so pick a manifest that lives somewhere you're fine having edited -- not a read-only reference copy. This field also accepts a glob (e.g. 'manifests/*.csv') to launch one parallel task per matching file, though a single-file picker UI may not offer a way to type a glob -- use the CLI or 'enter path manually' option if your launcher only lets you browse to one file. Its h5ad_path column locates the data only when nothing overrides it -- see 'h5ad' below, needed on platforms that don't mount arbitrary manifest-referenced paths into the task.

h5ad.description: Override the manifest's h5ad_path column with this file.
h5ad.help_text: Needed on ICA and similar platforms that don't mount a project's data tree into the task container -- a path typed into the manifest (relative or absolute) resolves to nothing there; only a file passed as an actual pipeline input (this one) gets staged in. Leave blank on a local/HPC run where the manifest's own h5ad_path is already reachable from wherever the task executes.

dragen_root.description: One or more directories containing runs' DRAGEN output subfolders, for the report's Sequencing QC section.
dragen_root.help_text: Optional -- everything else in the report works without it. Each subfolder must be named the same way the manifest's own dragen_path values already end (their basename); this overrides every run's dragen_path to whichever <a root>/<that basename> actually exists, trying every root given here for every run. Several roots are for when runs' DRAGEN output doesn't share one common parent directory -- for the same reason --h5ad exists, this platform doesn't mount project data into the task, so the manifest's own dragen_path values resolve to nothing on their own. On the CLI, pass multiple paths space-separated after one --dragen_root. Leaving this blank just skips the Sequencing QC section -- not an error.

qc_container.description: Container image to run every step in.
qc_container.help_text: Defaults to the published image (Google Artifact Registry, public -- verified pullable with zero credentials, so ICA and any other executor can reach it like a public Docker Hub image), built from containers/Dockerfile via containers/build_and_push_gcp.sh. This isn't read via a Nextflow profile -- ICA (and most cloud/container-native executors) does not reliably apply profiles, so RUN_QC_REPORT's container directive reads this parameter directly instead. Only override it if you've rebuilt and pushed your own copy (containers/SETUP.md covers both the GCP and AWS ECR paths). Leave blank only for a genuinely container-free run (conda or bare metal with the dependencies already installed).

outdir.description: Where reports, figures and tables are published.
outdir.help_text: Each manifest gets its own subfolder here, named after the manifest's filename (without extension): <outdir>/<manifest-name>/analysis_outputs/. The manifest's own 'output_path' column is not used for this -- it's ignored so results land in Nextflow's own output tree instead of wherever the manifest happened to point.

publish_mode.description: How published files are placed in --outdir (Nextflow publishDir mode).

run_mode_options.title: Run mode
run_mode_options.description: The pipeline is explore-first: a manifest with no QC thresholds set stops after QC review by default, and needs to be run a second time (after the thresholds are filled in) to produce the full report.

mode.description: default: let the manifest's threshold state decide (explore first, full once thresholds are set). explore: always stop after QC. auto: skip the review step, run end-to-end on thresholds derived from the data.

qc_threshold_options.title: QC thresholds
qc_threshold_options.description: Per-cell QC gates. Leave all five blank to have them derived from the data (recommended for a first pass -- see 'mode' above). These override anything already set in the manifest.

min_genes.description: Minimum genes detected per cell. Leave blank to derive from the data.

max_genes.description: Maximum genes detected per cell. Leave blank to derive from the data.

min_counts.description: Minimum total UMI counts per cell. Leave blank to derive from the data.

max_counts.description: Maximum total UMI counts per cell. Leave blank to derive from the data.

max_mito.description: Maximum percent mitochondrial reads. Leave blank to derive from the data.

transcriptome_options.title: Transcriptome / clustering options
transcriptome_options.description: Normalisation, embedding and clustering. All optional; the defaults match a typical single-condition Perturb-seq run.

counts_layer.description: Read raw counts from adata.layers[NAME] instead of X.
counts_layer.help_text: Use when X holds normalised or log-transformed values and raw counts live in a named layer.

subsample_cells.description: Randomly subsample to at most N cells after loading.
subsample_cells.help_text: Escape hatch for a very large experiment that won't fit in memory. The report states the subsample size prominently, since per-perturbation cell counts scale down with it.

conditions.description: Manifest columns to use as comparison axes, space-separated (e.g. 'fixation gRNA_method'). Leave blank to autodetect.

doublets.help_text: Off by default: scrublet assumes a heterogeneous population, so its scores aren't informative for a homogeneous line, and per-batch it is memory-hungry. Doublets are never dropped either way, only flagged.

regress_qc.description: Regress sequencing depth and %mito out of the embedding.
regress_qc.help_text: Off by default: it only ever affects clusters/UMAP/E-distance (never DE results) and is the longest step in the stage. Cell-cycle regression is deliberately not offered as an option -- many knockouts are proliferation phenotypes, and regressing out cell-cycle scores would suppress exactly the perturbations being screened for.

batch_correct.help_text: 'harmony' corrects the PCA, which propagates to clusters, UMAP AND the E-distance effect sizes in the perturbation section -- refused if the resolved batch key is also a declared condition column, since that would integrate away the comparison the experiment is designed to measure.

hvg_batch_key.description: Make highly-variable-gene selection batch-aware on this manifest column.
hvg_batch_key.help_text: Off by default. Do not point it at a condition column -- with seurat_v3 this de-prioritises genes that differ between levels of that column, which is the opposite of what you want when the column IS the comparison.

n_top_genes.description: Number of highly variable genes (tool default: 5000).

n_marker_genes.description: Top marker genes per cluster shown in the marker dot plot (tool default: 5).

cluster_col.description: Name of an existing obs column holding cluster labels, to reuse instead of reclustering.
cluster_col.help_text: Reusing an existing embedding requires PCA, UMAP AND a recognised cluster column all to be present. If your cluster column's name isn't one of the built-in candidates (leiden, leiden_clusters, louvain, clusters, leiden_gpu) and isn't given here, the pipeline can't tell clustering was already done and recomputes the whole embedding.

force_recompute.description: Ignore QC metrics, embedding, clustering and doublet calls already present in the h5ad; recompute everything from raw counts.

low_memory.description: Trade speed for peak memory (skips copying the input matrix, smaller DE gene blocks).

skip_input_check.description: Skip the plausibility check that the expression matrix is real gene expression.
skip_input_check.help_text: Only for a matrix you've already validated by other means -- this check exists because a var_names/X column permutation produced two confident, wrong reports before anyone thought to ask whether ACTB was detected.

guide_calling_options.title: Guide calling
guide_calling_options.description: How guide-RNA assignment decides which guide (if any) a cell carries.

guide_min_reads.description: Minimum guide UMIs for a cell to be eligible for assignment (tool default: 10).

guide_purity_min.description: Minimum top1/(top1+top2) percent required to assign a guide (tool default: 75).

dual_guide.description: Force dual-guide (iBAR) handling. Leave unset to autodetect from guide-ID structure (the tool default, and correct for almost every library).
dual_guide.help_text: This maps to a true/false/unset parameter in nextflow.config (unset = autodetect, true = force dual-guide, false = force single-guide) that a checkbox can only imperfectly represent: a checkbox that is left untouched may still be submitted as 'false' by some launchers, which would force single-guide instead of autodetecting. If that happens on your platform, use 'extra_args' with --dual-guide or --single-guide instead of this field, or leave this hidden section alone entirely and let the tool autodetect (the recommended default for essentially every library).

hashtag_options.title: Hashtags
hashtag_options.description: Hashtag demultiplexing thresholding, when the experiment used cell hashing.

hto_threshold_mode.description: How the per-hashtag positivity threshold is chosen.

hto_quantile.description: Background quantile used as the threshold when hto_threshold_mode is background_quantile (tool default: 0.99).

report_options.title: Report
report_options.description: Controls over the HTML report itself.

title.description: Report title. Defaults to the experiment ID guessed from the manifest/output path.

link_figures.description: Link figures instead of embedding them.
link_figures.help_text: Produces a smaller HTML file, but the report is then no longer a single portable file -- the figures/ folder has to travel with it.

no_tables.description: Omit data tables from the HTML (the CSVs are still written to tables/).

max_de_targets.description: Cap on perturbations sent to differential expression (tool default: 40).

slides_options.title: Slide deck
slides_options.description: A Google-Slides-ready .pptx (analysis_outputs/qc_deck.pptx), built from the same registry the HTML report renders from. On by default.

build_slides.help_text: On by default. artifacts.json is still written either way, so you can build one manually later even if you turn this off -- see perturbseq_report_v1.3.5/build_slides.py.

slides_extra_args.description: Any build_slides.py flag(s) with no dedicated option here, passed through verbatim.

advanced_options.title: Advanced / escape hatches
advanced_options.description: For cases the options above don't cover. Most users will never need these.

config.description: JSON or YAML file of perturbseq_report configuration overrides.
config.help_text: For settings with no dedicated option here -- anything in perturbseq_report's PipelineConfig dataclasses (see the vendored package's config.py).

extra_args.description: Any other perturbseq-report CLI flag(s), passed through verbatim.

pipeline_dir.description: Where the vendored perturbseq_report package lives. Computed automatically from qc_container -- do not edit unless you know why.

help.description: Print the CLI help message and exit.
